data.narrative:
Kraken Robotics is a publicly listed company in the Defense & Security sector. The comparable universe consists of 2 public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private competitors, including Evolv Technology, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic. This represents a constrained set within a sector that contains 21 same-stage peers overall.

Peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The Defense & Security universe lacks sufficient narrow-filter comparables; only 1 same-stage peer was identified, with zero adjacent-stage and zero similar-tier matches. This falls short of the three-datapoint minimum required for reliable peer triangulation. An all-sector median approach would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneous risk, margin, and growth profiles across Defense & Security subsegments.

Without a sufficiently populated comparable set or disclosed multiples from the top private peers, traditional valuation methods cannot be reliably applied. Practitioners should supplement this analysis with revenue run-rate analysis, contract backlog assessment, and customer concentration metrics specific to Kraken's business. Given the public listing status and thin peer coverage, direct market capitalization observation combined with fundamental cash-flow or FCF analysis would provide more grounded valuation anchors than cross-sector comps. Key uncertainties remain around government procurement concentration, defense spending cycles, and the competitive positioning versus the identified private cohort.
